summary:
Iran’s military said it attacked a US military base in Bahrain on Sunday, the second time it has targeted the country in three days. Bahrain’s air-defence force said it thwarted several Iranian aerial attacks. Bahrain is home to the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, and the latest claims came as strikes resumed in the Gulf.

A nationwide US flight stoppage lasted nearly five hours, disrupting thousands of flights and potentially affecting more than a million travellers. The Trump administration blamed problems with overloaded systems and faulty equipment during work to replace old copper communication wires. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the disruption was tied to maintenance or an error by the contractor; officials warned that it could take days for travel to return to normal. President Volodymyr Zelensky said US negotiators had floated Ukraine withdrawing from Donbas in exchange for NATO membership. The US has not confirmed the proposal, while a US official said many ideas were still being discussed.

The United States has lost its measles-elimination status after 26 years, the Pan American Health Organization reportedly said. The CDC has confirmed 5,412 measles cases in 2026, more than double last year’s total and the highest number since 1991. The status change comes as the country faces its worst outbreaks in more than three decades.

headlines.title: Jordan sentences three men to death over church attack
headlines.summary: A Jordanian court sentenced three men to death for a gun attack on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church. The attack killed nine people; reports said 25 or 34 others were injured.

headlines.title: South Sudan delays its first national election
headlines.summary: South Sudan has pushed back its planned national election, which would be the first since independence in 2011. The vote had been scheduled for December, and analysts had warned it faced a legitimacy crisis.

headlines.title: SpaceX catches Starship at its Texas launchpad
headlines.summary: SpaceX recovered Starship at its south Texas launchpad, guiding the vehicle between mechanical arms on the launch tower. The company called it a first-ever catch and a milestone in efforts to make rocket systems fully reusable.
